canonical_task: CFL membership is P-complete
citation: Jones & Laaser (1976); GHR (1995)

canonical_task: k-HDS is P-complete for k>=3 (in NC for k<=2)
citation: Anderson & Mayr (1984); GHR (1995)

canonical_task: Datalog data complexity is P-complete
citation: Immerman/Vardi; Dantsin-Eiter-Gottlob-Voronkov (2001)

canonical_task: GE with partial pivoting is P-complete (unlike determinant/linear-equations, which are in NC)
citation: Vavasis (1989)

canonical_task: resource-graph reduction, poly-time
citation: Spirakis, The parallel complexity of deadlock detection (1986); GHR (1995)

canonical_task: constraint-based type inference via unification, poly-time (simply-typed)
citation: O'Toole & Gifford; Dwork, Kanellakis & Mitchell (1984)

canonical_task: LFMIS membership: computable greedily in polynomial time
citation: Cook, A taxonomy of problems with fast parallel algorithms, Information and Control 64 (1985); via Greenlaw, Hoover & Ruzzo, Limits to Parallel Computation (1995)
note: in P (sequential greedy). Distinct from independent-set (lex-first selection object, S2)

canonical_task: Vertex-Guard decision: do k vertex guards cover the polygon?
citation: Lee & Lin, Computational complexity of art gallery problems, IEEE Trans. Inform. Theory 32 (1986) 276-282
note: vertex/edge-guard art gallery is NP-hard (Lee-Lin 1986). Vertex-guard variant is pinned to stay in NP

canonical_task: Bounded PCP decision: a matching index sequence of length <= k?
citation: Garey & Johnson, Computers and Intractability (1979) [Bounded PCP, SR11]; classical (Constable-Hunt-Sahni)
note: the length-bounded PCP is NP-complete (unbounded PCP is undecidable). Distinct from the unbounded PCP (S2)

canonical_task: Cluster Deletion decision: make G a cluster graph by deleting <= k edges?
citation: Shamir, Sharan & Tsur, Cluster graph modification problems, Discrete Appl. Math. 144 (2004) 173-182
note: NP-complete (Shamir-Sharan-Tsur 2004). Distinct from Cluster Editing (add+delete) and Cluster Vertex Deletion (delete vertices) (S2)

canonical_task: Domatic Number decision: does V partition into >= k disjoint dominating sets?
citation: Garey & Johnson, Computers and Intractability (1979) [Domatic Number, GT3]; Bonuccelli (1985)
note: NP-complete (deciding domatic number >= 3). Distinct from Domination Number (S2)

canonical_task: Max-GAP decision: total profit >= t within capacities? NP-complete (generalizes 0/1 knapsack and bin packing)
citation: Garey & Johnson, Computers and Intractability (1979)

canonical_task: Minimum t-Spanner decision (t=2): 2-spanner with <= k edges? NP-complete
citation: Peleg & Schaffer, Graph spanners, Journal of Graph Theory 13 (1989) 99-116

canonical_task: min-size k-ECSS decision: spanning k-edge-connected subgraph with <= t edges? NP-complete (2-ECSS contains Hamiltonicity)
citation: Garey & Johnson, Computers and Intractability (1979)
note: 2-edge-connected spanning subgraph generalizes Hamiltonian cycle -> NP-complete

canonical_task: MAX-k-CUT decision: a k-partition cutting >= t edges? NP-complete (k=2 is MAX-CUT)
citation: Garey, Johnson & Stockmeyer, Some simplified NP-complete graph problems, Theoretical Computer Science 1 (1976) 237-267

canonical_task: minimum-max-degree spanning tree decision: spanning tree of max degree <= k? (k=2 is Hamiltonian Path)
citation: Garey & Johnson, Computers and Intractability (1979) [Hamiltonian Path, ND1]
note: k=2 restriction is Hamiltonian Path -> NP-complete

canonical_task: Minimum Distance decision: a nonzero codeword of weight <= d?
citation: Vardy, The intractability of computing the minimum distance of a code, IEEE Trans. Inform. Theory 43 (1997) 1757-1766
note: NP-hard (Vardy 1997), resolving the Berlekamp-McEliece-van Tilborg 1978 conjecture

canonical_task: MWT decision: a triangulation of total length <= L?
citation: Mulzer & Rote, Minimum-weight triangulation is NP-hard, JACM 55(2) (2008) Art. 11 (arXiv:cs/0601002)
note: NP-hard (Mulzer-Rote 2008), a long-standing open problem from Garey-Johnson (1979)

canonical_task: Book Thickness decision: a book embedding using <= k pages?
citation: Chung, Leighton & Rosenberg, Embedding graphs in books: a layout problem with applications to VLSI design, SIAM J. Algebraic Discrete Methods 8 (1987) 33-58
note: NP-complete; testing pagenumber <= 2 is already NP-complete (a graph has a 2-page embedding iff it is subhamiltonian)

canonical_task: Precoloring Extension decision: does the precoloring extend to a proper coloring with the given colors?
citation: Biró, Hujter & Tuza, Precoloring extension. I. Interval graphs, Discrete Math. 100 (1992) 267-279

canonical_task: Register Sufficiency: DAG evaluable with <= k registers?
citation: Sethi, Complete register allocation problems, SIAM J. Comput. 4 (1975) 226-248
note: Sethi-Ullman labeling is optimal on trees; the general-DAG problem is NP-complete

canonical_task: Transposition distance decision: sortable in <= k transpositions?
citation: Bulteau, Fertin & Rusu, Sorting by transpositions is difficult, SIAM J. Discrete Math. 26 (2012) 1148-1180

canonical_task: Target Set Selection decision: a seed set of size <= k activating all vertices?
citation: Chen, On the approximability of influence in social networks, SIAM J. Discrete Math. 23 (2009) 1400-1415

canonical_task: UFP decision: route a demand subset of total value >= V on single paths within capacities?
citation: Kleinberg, Approximation algorithms for disjoint paths problems (PhD thesis, MIT 1996)

canonical_task: existence of a contingency table with margins (r,c): feasible iff sum(r)=sum(c), and a witness is built in poly time by the northwest-corner rule — the (easy) transportation-feasibility decoupling witness
citation: Dantzig, Linear Programming and Extensions, Princeton Univ. Press (1963)
note: northwest-corner construction / transportation-polytope feasibility (sum(r)=sum(c)); existence is elementary

canonical_task: #spanning-trees via the Matrix-Tree cofactor = a determinant, which is in NC
citation: Csanky, Fast parallel matrix inversion algorithms, SIAM J. Comput. 5(4) (1976) 618-623
note: the Laplacian cofactor is a determinant, in NC (Csanky 1976 / Berkowitz 1984) (F-4); mirrors planar-matching-count
